entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained in direction; level unexplained (fincorp-34; the sources disagree). K_BANK <- E_BANK K2a private, 2,30,814 -> 2,05,682 (-25,132, -10.9%; z 0.891; free low; binding: k2.fc_saving_total (target 9,91,448, balanced 9,91,449, at its upper edge); k2.private (target 4,55,938, balanced 4,55,939, at its upper edge)). E_BANK ran a -1,02,838 deficit and E_NBFC a 2,32,893 surplus in the prior (fincorp-2): FISIM leaves banks' SNA property income negative, while the F4a GOS split (NAS 8.12 S125-S127 GVA, including MFs, auxiliaries and captive institutions) gives NBFCs more GOS than the RTP-scaled interest matrix can carry. K2a is a GOS-proportional split of NAS 1.9 FC saving (no sub-sector data; free, low; the public and private totals held by k2.*), so balancing moved saving from banks to NBFCs. FSF supports that direction: capital_financial's nas_vs_fsf is 3,68,035 for banks (NAS-based saving above FSF net lending) and -1,34,403 for NBFCs. RBI Trend and Progress business accounts oppose it (banks' saving near 4.6 lakh, NBFCs' near 1.5 lakh before auxiliaries and captives; fincorp-2). Which source to follow is a Checkpoint B decision. GRAS (no weights, no constraints) gives 2,23,525. The prior account gaps (BALANCING.md 'Pre-balancing imbalances'; closure institution_gaps): G_STA 4,50,426, households Z -3,84,547, E_NFPU 3,12,829, G_CEN -2,98,948, E_NBFC 2,32,893, E_INSP -1,21,568, E_NFPR -1,13,892, E_BANK -1,02,838, E_RBI 25,646.

entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained. K_GCEN <- G_CEN K3a saving_neg, -3,42,973 -> -4,30,437 (-87,464, -25.5%; z 1.255; free low; binding: gov.k3.gg_saving (target -3,18,384, balanced -3,18,384, at its upper edge)). The K3a priors split NAS 2026 St 1.9 GG saving (held by gov.k3.gg_saving) by the treasury cash bridge (government-2, -25). The prior leaves G_CEN -2,98,948 (short) and G_STA 4,50,426 (long); once the Wave C constraints held the published transfer totals (NAS 4.2 COFOG current transfers, R9d, R18, the outside-treasury CSS money, the Union's R10 lines), the saving split became the main outlet: the Centre's saving went -3,39,090 -> -4,27,343 and the States' 20,705 -> 1,08,959. Independent FSF evidence supports the direction: capital_financial's k9_decomposition term nas_vs_fsf is 1,42,584 for the Centre (NAS-based saving less GCF above its FSF net lending) and -1,97,779 for the States, so FSF puts the Centre lower and the States higher by about those amounts; the balanced split moves part of the way. The saving_pos / saving_neg pair of each government moves together (a sign-fragile net written as two entries). GRAS (no weights, no constraints) gives -3,49,733.

entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained. Cell K_GCEN <- I_GSEC: 11,53,484 -> 11,71,445 (17,961, +1.6%; 5 entries). Largest moves: capital_financial K8 dom_keyed_pos 15,277 (+3.4%); capital_financial K8 dom_pos 1,349 (+0.2%); capital_financial K7b row_cp_fpi_debt_gsec 989 (+0.8%); capital_financial K7b hh_cp 193 (+0.8%); capital_financial K8 dom_neg 153 (+0.2%). The largest mover is explained under its entry: The GG and FC capital accounts close through their saving priors, which balancing moved (K3a: the Centre down, the States up, toward FSF; K2a: banks down, NBFCs up). The GFCF, G-sec and loan totals are held (cf.i1a.gfcf.gg, production's gfcf.c_cnst, the cf.k8.* issuance totals), so only this block's keys can move: the Centre/State GFCF key (capital_financial-11, which leaves out ULB capital expenditure 1,07,404 and CSS spending outside State treasuries, both of which point the same way) and the issuer-vs-holder G-sec and deposit splits (capital_financial-29). The moves are a few per cent.

entries.why: Explained (the move; the group profile it keeps is finding BS-8). K_HH <- H_R1 K4a total, 3,32,439 -> 3,54,374 (21,935, +6.6%; z 1.066; free low; binding: cf.k4.hh_saving (target 58,90,330, balanced 58,90,330, at its lower edge)). The prior K4a is each group's current-account residual (closure option A); the ten residuals sum to 55,05,784 against NAS 2026 St 1.9 household saving 58,90,330 (Z = -3,84,547; check k4.prior_sum_vs_nas), and cf.k4.hh_saving binds at its lower edge. The other blocks' flows delivered households too little income (closure institution_gaps), and cross-entropy closed Z mostly by raising households' property income (R8a) and cutting their interest payments (R5), which raises every group's saving by 6-8% of its prior. The level by group inherits the factor-income keys' shape (D2-19, factors-19): rural groups save more than urban ones, the reverse of IFPRI 2022/23; that is an owner decision for Checkpoint B (closure-19, BS-8), not something balancing can settle. GRAS (no weights, no constraints) gives 3,42,030.

entries.label: balancing_set
entries.why: Explained in direction; level unexplained (fincorp-34; the sources disagree). K_NBFC <- E_NBFC K2a private, 1,82,060 -> 2,17,059 (34,999, +19.2%; z 1.192; free low; binding: k2.fc_saving_total (target 9,91,448, balanced 9,91,449, at its upper edge); k2.private (target 4,55,938, balanced 4,55,939, at its upper edge)). E_BANK ran a -1,02,838 deficit and E_NBFC a 2,32,893 surplus in the prior (fincorp-2): FISIM leaves banks' SNA property income negative, while the F4a GOS split (NAS 8.12 S125-S127 GVA, including MFs, auxiliaries and captive institutions) gives NBFCs more GOS than the RTP-scaled interest matrix can carry. K2a is a GOS-proportional split of NAS 1.9 FC saving (no sub-sector data; free, low; the public and private totals held by k2.*), so balancing moved saving from banks to NBFCs. FSF supports that direction: capital_financial's nas_vs_fsf is 3,68,035 for banks (NAS-based saving above FSF net lending) and -1,34,403 for NBFCs. RBI Trend and Progress business accounts oppose it (banks' saving near 4.6 lakh, NBFCs' near 1.5 lakh before auxiliaries and captives; fincorp-2). Which source to follow is a Checkpoint B decision. GRAS (no weights, no constraints) gives 2,00,695. The prior account gaps (BALANCING.md 'Pre-balancing imbalances'; closure institution_gaps): G_STA 4,50,426, households Z -3,84,547, E_NFPU 3,12,829, G_CEN -2,98,948, E_NBFC 2,32,893, E_INSP -1,21,568, E_NFPR -1,13,892, E_BANK -1,02,838, E_RBI 25,646.
